court: Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit

issues.label: Standard and scope of review
issues.why: Court must determine whether it reviews IJ or BIA decision and applies substantial-evidence versus de novo review to each finding.

issues.label: Which decision to review
issues.why: BIA adopted and affirmed the IJ, so the court must decide the scope of reviewable reasoning from both bodies.

issues.label: Exhaustion of PSG claims
issues.why: Court must determine whether 'Salvadoran women' and 'family members of witnesses' were properly raised below and thus reviewable.

issues.label: Waiver/forfeiture of arguments on appeal
issues.why: BIA declined to reach two PSGs as raised in first instance, implicating whether those claims are preserved.

issues.label: Political opinion as protected ground
issues.why: Court must assess whether opposition to violence/rule-of-law qualifies and whether applicant actually holds it.

issues.label: Imputed political opinion
issues.why: Court must consider whether persecutor imputed a political opinion to applicant regardless of her actual beliefs.

issues.label: Nexus 'one central reason' standard for asylum
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether protected ground was at least one central reason for persecution.

issues.label: Mixed-motive analysis
issues.why: Persecutor may act from personal revenge and protected-ground motives simultaneously, requiring mixed-motive assessment.

issues.label: Family as cognizable particular social group
issues.why: Nuclear family membership is often a paradigmatic PSG requiring proper nexus analysis.

issues.label: Nexus to nuclear-family PSG
issues.why: Court must decide if familial relationship to Porfiria was a central reason for feared harm.

issues.label: Cognizability of gender-based PSGs
issues.why: Whether 'Salvadoran women' and 'females viewed as property' are legally cognizable social groups.

issues.label: Nexus to gender-based PSGs
issues.why: Court must review whether harm was on account of gender given abuse of male relatives too.

issues.label: Membership in prosecutorial-witness PSG
issues.why: Court must decide whether applicant or J.P.A. qualify as family of witnesses given the discounted identification.

issues.label: Past persecution finding
issues.why: Court must determine whether threats and machete incident constitute past persecution triggering presumption.

issues.label: Presumption of future persecution
issues.why: Established past persecution would shift burden to government to rebut future fear.

issues.label: Well-founded fear of future persecution
issues.why: Court must assess objective and subjective components independently of past persecution.

issues.label: Government unwillingness/inability to protect
issues.why: Private actor persecution requires showing the state cannot or will not protect the applicant.

issues.label: Internal relocation feasibility
issues.why: Court must consider whether safe relocation within El Salvador is possible and reasonable.

issues.label: Withholding of removal standard
issues.why: Higher 'clear probability' standard under INA must be separately evaluated.

issues.label: CAT likelihood of torture
issues.why: Court must assess whether applicant showed more-likely-than-not risk of torture.

issues.label: Government acquiescence for CAT
issues.why: Whether failure to prosecute and open investigation constitute acquiescence or willful blindness.

issues.label: Nexus not required for CAT
issues.why: Court must recognize CAT does not require a protected-ground nexus, unlike asylum.

issues.label: Derivative applicant J.P.A.'s status
issues.why: J.P.A.'s claim depends on principal but may have independent CAT considerations.

issues.label: Consideration of country-conditions evidence
issues.why: Court must ensure documentary evidence of El Salvador conditions was properly weighed.

issues.label: Whether IJ ignored material evidence
issues.why: Applicant alleges the IJ ignored evidence, requiring review of factfinding completeness.

issues.label: Single-member BIA decision adequacy
issues.why: Court must assess whether the streamlined BIA decision provided sufficient reasoning for review.
